subject: Inference edge topology & egress hardening — readout and action items
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@horizonhealth.com>, Claire Nunez <claire@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Readout: inference edge topology and egress hardening (action list)

Hi Sanjay / Claire,

Thanks for taking the time this morning. As promised, here's the readout from our topology session and a proposed set of concrete actions for the HorizonHealth private deployment. High-level goals we aligned on: keep inference latency under 50ms p90 for edge traffic, ensure all egress leaves via Horizon-managed egress points, and maintain auditable control-plane telemetry without exposing control APIs across customer VNets.

Summary (short):
- Control plane: Redwood control-plane components will live in a dedicated management VPC (Redwood-managed control plane endpoints). Only customer-side (Horizon) control-plane agents will have a bi-directional mTLS channel to those endpoints over a pinned endpoint (PrivateLink-backed).
- Data plane (inference): Model-serving nodes stay inside Horizon's private VPCs. We recommend colocating GPU inference pools in the same AZs to avoid cross-AZ egress charges and latency spikes.
- Egress: All outbound external traffic (metrics, model pull from S3, OS updates if allowed) must traverse Horizon egress collectors; no direct internet egress from inference nodes. We'll support either NAT GW via controlled subnets or explicit egress proxies.

Requested next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Marcus: Push updated draw.io with annotated subnets & PrivateLink endpoints (attached) — ETA EOD today.
2) Kimberly: Provide concrete ACL and security group snippets for the inferred topology — ETA 08/06.
3) Jonas & Irene: Validate control-plane audit retention and what events Redwood will send to Horizon SIEM (list out event types) — ETA 08/06.
4) Sanjay / NetEng: Confirm whether Horizon will accept TLS SNI-based routing to the management endpoint or needs an L4 pass-through — ETA 08/05.

Attachments: hh_inference_topology_v1.drawio (diagram), egress_matrix.xlsx (egress policy matrix), network_acl_snippets.txt (example ACLs).

If anything above looks off, flag now. Otherwise I'll PR the diagram and ACL snippets into the shared Drive and update INF-919 to track the work.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Nunez <claire@horizonhealth.com>, HorizonHealth NetEng <neteng@horizonhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:44:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Readout: inference edge topology and egress hardening (action list)

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. A couple of clarifying Qs from NetEng after the call: 

1) PrivateLink vs. L4 pass-through: Our infra team prefers PrivateLink for control-plane endpoints because it avoids extra hairpin routing. However we need to confirm that Redwood will accept client IP preservation or if the management API logs will show the PrivateLink VPC ENI IP instead. Can you confirm what will appear in your control-plane access logs?

2) Egress for model pulls: We want to centralize model downloads to a dedicated bastion subnet that has access to the internet through a monitored NAT and can be rate-limited. Can Redwood's model distribution agent be reconfigured to pull from a Horizon S3 mirror via presigned URLs and respect retry/backoff?

3) Audit / telemetry: We're asking for a minimal event set that will be emitted to our SIEM: control-plane auth events, model-pull initiation/complete, instance lifecycle (start/stop/crash), and config-change events. Can you outline retention windows?

If we can get short answers here we'll mark this as ready for the security review board.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Sr. NetEng, HorizonHealth

---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@horizonhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Claire Nunez <claire@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:03:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Readout: inference edge topology and egress hardening (action list)

Sanjay — quick answers inline below: 

1) PrivateLink visibility: When clients connect via AWS PrivateLink the control-plane receiver sees connections from the ENI IP inside our management VPC. We will include the originating VPC/customer identifier in the access logs (we add a connection-origin tag during auth handshake). You will not see the originating private IP of the inference node by default; if you need source IP we can add it but it requires explicit consent (we'd include it in audit events and store under restricted retention).

2) Model pulls: Yes — Redwood agents can be configured to pull from customer-hosted S3 mirrors using presigned URLs. The agent supports configurable backoff and concurrency limits. We'll include a config flag in the agent release that Horizon can set during onboarding.

3) Telemetry retention: By default Redwood keeps control-plane auth and lifecycle events for 90 days in the hosted control-plane; we can extend to 365 days under enterprise retention with additional export to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/forwarder). For the private deployment scenario we can push the minimal event set to your collector in near-real-time (sub-second batching) — specifics in the ACL doc.

I'll draft the exact event list and retention options and drop into INF-919.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal PM, Platform Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@horizonhealth.com>, Claire Nunez <claire@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Updated diagrams and ACL snippets (per action items)

Folks — attaching the updated files per our commitments. Key changes in v1.1 of the diagram: 
- Annotated PrivateLink endpoint (managed endpoint name: rp-control-us-west-2.redwood.internal)
- Dedicated model-batch egress subnet and recommended NAT placement (to avoid inference node ephemeral egress)
- Explicit SIEM forwarder endpoint (TLS, client cert) in the management VPC

Snippets in network_acl_snippets.txt cover the following:
- Security group examples restricting port 8443 (control-plane API) to the PrivateLink ENI CIDR and Horizon NetEng CIDR
- Egress rules for the model-bastion subnet permitting S3 presigned URL outbound only, and blocking outbound 22/23 for image pulls

I also added a fallback policy: if Horizon cannot host an S3 mirror, Redwood will use a signed, short-lived model artifact delivery from us but only after both parties approve the SLA for bandwidth and storage egress.

Attachments: hh_inference_topology_v1.drawio (diagram v1.1), network_acl_snippets.txt, egress_matrix.xlsx

Action items updated in INF-919; please review and ack.

-marcus

Thanks Marcus and team — diagrams look good and the ACL snippets give our infra team something actionable. A couple quick confirmations: 

- We will do PrivateLink for control-plane (ok).
- We'll host the S3 mirror; Claire to share bucket naming and an initial presigned URL process doc by 08/06.
- Please make sure the access logs include the connection-origin tag that Irene mentioned — that's a must for our SOC.

Sanjay and NetEng will review the ACLs tomorrow and we'll open any follow-ups in INF-919. If nothing else, consider this thread confirmed and moving to security review board.

Claire
Claire Nunez
Director, Infrastructure Security, HorizonHealth
